newsitem.title: BRAZIL: African trade group seeks ties with Mercosur.
newsitem.headline: African trade group seeks ties with Mercosur.

text.p: The executive secretary of the Southern African Development Community (SADC) was in Brazil on Tuesday to forge ties between the African trade group and South America's Mercosur customs union, officials said.
A Brazilian Foreign Ministry official said Kaire Mbuende would hold talks with Brazilian officials in the capital Brasilia before flying on for a one-day visit to Sao Paulo.
"The visit's purpose is to examine the possibility of closer ties between SADC and Mercosur, in particular, Brazil," the ministry said in a statement.

Mercosur groups Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay in a trade bloc comprising some 200 million people. The 12-member SADC envisages a regional trade grouping in Southern Africa with some 150 million people.
South African President Nelson Mandela said on Tuesday during a visit to Brunei that SADC should also establish closer links with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).
The Brazilian Foreign Ministry official, asking not to be named, said SADC executive secretary Mbuende would travel to Uruguay on Thursday.
